payload.writeUp: Deep dive E of 24 October 2026: a fresh look at 21 UK companies already in the pool, re-checking from their own sites, Companies House, platform listings and the press whether each is genuinely raising now, closed, or unknown. candidate.name: OSSTEC
candidate.teaser: Imperial spin-out making 3D-printed cementless partial knee implants; £4m EIS round open on Wealth Club, first close 30 Oct 2026.
candidate.description: OSSTEC Ltd (Companies House 13500695, incorporated 8 Jul 2021) is an Imperial College London spin-out developing ASCENT, a 3D-printed, press-fit (cementless) partial knee implant supplied with CLARITY instrumentation. Wealth Club is running a single-company EIS offer (page dated 16 Oct 2026): £4m sought, £3.5m already committed by Embryo Ventures, New Wave Ventures, OTIF, Empirical Ventures and SFC Capital, £500k Wealth Club allocation, £16.8m pre-money (fully diluted) at £8.42 per share, minimum £20,616, first close 5pm 30 Oct 2026. The company is pre-revenue (FY to July 2026); FDA 510(k) submission is expected Q4 2026 with clearance hoped for in H1 2027. Earlier: £2.5m round led by Empirical Ventures (Apr 2025). Companies House shows a dense run of SH01 allotments Nov 2024 to Jun 2025 and two charges registered Aug 2025. Founder and CEO is Max (Maxwell) Munford; directors also include Dr Jonathan Jeffers and Dominique Kleyn. Risks: regulatory clearance not guaranteed, pre-revenue, £16.8m valuation is high for a family cheque, forecasts are the company's own.
